dataset_description: Checked-in wording-variance challenge pack used to keep softer suspicion language, optional follow-up recommendations, and inflammatory confounders visible in the public proof surface.
labeling_policy: This deidentified repository sample emphasizes reviewer-visible pancreatic concern, follow-up language, and confounder handling rather than autonomous diagnostic claims. Labels were shaped to preserve the ambiguity a reviewer would still need to inspect.
notes: Repository challenge pack for public proof only. This is not a clinical validation dataset.
notable_strengths: Top-ranked positives still cluster around the most actionable lesion and occult-lesion concern cases.
The pack keeps softer wording and optional-sounding follow-up recommendations visible in the same reviewer-facing proof shape.
known_limitations: Sample remains small and deidentified for repository use.
One optional-sounding follow-up case remains missed and one pancreatitis confounder remains overcalled.

cohort_descriptions.description: Front-door CT cases where softer phrasing and inflammatory change can blur the line between a true pancreatic cue and a confounder.
Surveillance MRI cases centered on cyst follow-up language, interval wording, and optional-sounding reimaging recommendations.
Navigator-style review cases that mix high-acuity lesion language, equivocal focal fullness, and clearly benign negatives.

benchmark_bucket_descriptions.description: Reports with direct lesion or malignant-process wording that should remain easy to justify in a reviewed queue.
Cases driven by focal fullness, duct change, or hedged occult-lesion language instead of a direct mass declaration.
Operationally important pancreatic follow-up recommendations that can sound optional enough to miss.
Specificity checks where inflammatory duct prominence risks being overcalled as a suspicious pancreatic signal.
Clearly nonsuspicious pancreatic reports that should stay out of the flagged queue.
